title: Editor colours
about: A terminal in whatever the editor is wearing, so the two panes are one surface rather than two windows that happen to touch. The background, the text and the cursor follow the theme in force — which is what `follows` says — while the sixteen ANSI colours are stated here, because ANSI still has to mean what ANSI means: red is red, and a failing test has to look like one. In daylight they used to sit at a middle lightness, on the argument that a terminal colour is as often a background as a foreground and has to take black text on top; measured on 2026-09-09, thirteen of the sixteen were under 4.5:1 as text on a light editor ground, which is how they are read in a prompt, a listing and a diff, and a user said the light terminal could not be used. They are darker now — each keeps its hue and clears 4.5:1 on every light editor ground the app ships — and a powerline segment in one of them wants light text, as it does in every light terminal palette.
